author: Vivian Chow
title: Man defrauded Claremont Colleges out of over $1 million through fraud scheme - NewsBreak
text:
By Vivian Chow No media credit provided. ,
1 hours ago
A man pleaded guilty to defrauding The Claremont Colleges out of over $1 million through a wire fraud scheme.
Steven Anthony Cowles, 45, of Santa Clarita, pleaded guilty to one count of wire fraud, the U.S. District Attorney’s Office announced Wednesday.
Cowles has been an electrical shop supervisor for The Claremont Colleges Services (TCCS) since 2015. He was responsible for maintaining the electrical components for all seven campuses across Los Angeles County, including ordering parts and supplies when needed.
From June 2018 to July 2024, Cowles embezzled approximately $1,000,571 from his employer through at least 1,343 unauthorized transactions, prosecutors said.
Cowles’ employer provided him with several Visa credit cards to purchase products and services related to his work and campus needs.
He linked his personal PayPal account to the company cards and would transfer funds from those cards to his personal account, court documents said.
To conceal the fraud scheme, he provided his employer with fake invoices and other forms that claimed to show the money transfers were legitimate purchases of electrical products and services.
Prosecutors said he used this method because “when transaction data was transmitted from Wells Fargo [cards] to Workday, the transaction would populate in the Workday system with only the name of the third-party payment platform, not the ultimate recipient of the funds,” court documents said.
On Jan. 7, Coles pleaded guilty to one count of wire fraud. A sentencing hearing is scheduled for April 22, where he faces up to 20 years in federal prison.
